name: Familiarity Detection Circuit
short_description: Accumulates evidence from perceptual fluency, schema matching strength, and exposure count to generate familiarity signals and recognition threshold transitions.

components.name: EVIDENCE_ACCUMULATOR
components.description: Integrates multiple sources of fluency and schema consistency evidence toward familiarity threshold

components.name: EXPOSURE_TRACKER
components.description: Monitors cumulative exposure count and decay over time

components.name: THRESHOLD_MONITOR
components.description: Detects when accumulated evidence reaches recognition threshold

components.name: FAMILIARITY_SIGNAL_GEN
components.description: Generates graded familiarity signal based on evidence level

key_references: Jacoby, L. L., & Dallas, M. (1981). On the relationship between autobiographical memory and perceptual learning. Journal of Experimental Psychology: General, 110(3), 306–340.
Whittlesea, B. W. (1993). Illusions of familiarity. Journal of Experimental Psychology: Learning, Memory, and Cognition, 19(6), 1235–1253.
design_implications: Repeated environmental exposure increases familiarity and comfort; design spaces for habitual use with consistent landmarks and spatial organization to facilitate fluency
Wayfinding systems benefit from gradual familiarization; provide redundant cues early in visitor journeys and reduce signage once spatial schemas are established
